name: Eggshell Blue
lede: Eggshell Blue is a very pale, cool blue-green named for a bird's eggshell; as a screen swatch it reads as a minty near-white.

sections.title: A dye name
sections.body: The name is old as a dye color. The Pigment Compendium notes a fifteenth-century manuscript, as read by Thompson in 1935, that lists a nightshade berry for dyeing *eggshell blue* [1]. The compendium only says the plant may be the one meant, so the identification is tentative [1].

sections.title: Blue or green?
sections.body: Our library finds the name in the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955, in the xkcd color survey of 2010 and in Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, which the ISCC-NBS cites [2]. Measured against the ISCC-NBS categories, the swatch is nearest to very light bluish green, 8.0 units of ΔE2000 away, so in that system it is more green than the name suggests [2]. Compare [[robin-s-egg-blue]], [[powder-blue]], [[mint-cream]] and [[eggshell-green]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The color is very rare in our archive: 2 paintings, 0.01 per cent of the total, as photographed [3]. The earlier of the two is by Vincent van Gogh, from 1888 [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [3].

origin.named_after: the shell of a bird's egg
origin.first_recorded: as a dye name, a fifteenth-century manuscript (per Thompson 1935)
